Native engine: categorical covariates

Source: vignettes/articles/model-native-factors.qmd

Use a factor, character or logical column as a covariate in syntax. Part of the Models collection, with the other native engine pages. This page needs the development version (0.11.0).

What it does replaces a categorical column on a regression’s right side with one 0/1 dummy per non-reference level
Class returned SEMFit
Syntax y ~ x + group, z*group_mid (label one dummy), group:m (one product per dummy)
Limit a categorical outcome, mediator or treatment is not supported (see Limits)

The page cuts covariate1 into three groups to have a factor to use:

library(medfit)

Attaching package: 'medfit'
The following object is masked from 'package:stats':

    decompose
library(generics)

Attaching package: 'generics'
The following objects are masked from 'package:base':

    as.difftime, as.factor, as.ordered, intersect, is.element, setdiff,
    setequal, union
dat <- transform(mediation_demo,
                 group = cut(covariate1, c(-Inf, -0.5, 0.5, Inf), labels = c("low", "mid", "high")))
base <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + group
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment + group
"

Fit and read it

Write group where a numeric covariate would go:

fit <- fit_sem(paste0(base, "ab := a * b"), dat)
tidy(fit)[1:7, c("term", "estimate", "std_error")]
# A tibble: 7 × 3
  term                 estimate std_error
  <chr>                   <dbl>     <dbl>
1 a                       0.549    0.102
2 mediator1~group_mid     0.328    0.125
3 mediator1~group_high    0.948    0.124
4 b                       0.618    0.0524
5 cp                      0.128    0.110
6 outcome~group_mid       0.463    0.132
7 outcome~group_high      0.729    0.139

group became group_mid and group_high, named <column>_<level>. The reference level is the first factor level (low), so each dummy is read against it. A character column is sorted in the C locale, so its reference does not depend on your session. A logical column gives one dummy, <column>_TRUE. The fit equals one with the dummies written by hand, and a, b and ab mean what they always mean.

Label or constrain one dummy

A label names one coefficient, so it goes on a dummy, never on the factor (b*group stops with a message that names the dummies). A constraint names a label:

pinned <- fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + group
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment + group + z * group_mid
  z == 0
", dat)
tidy(pinned)[grepl("group", tidy(pinned)$term, fixed = TRUE), c("term", "estimate")]
# A tibble: 8 × 2
  term                   estimate
  <chr>                     <dbl>
1 mediator1~group_mid      0.328
2 mediator1~group_high     0.948
3 outcome~group_high       0.474
4 treatment~~group_mid     0.0329
5 treatment~~group_high   -0.0359
6 group_mid~~group_mid     0.224
7 group_mid~~group_high   -0.118
8 group_high~~group_high   0.228

group_mid in the outcome equation is pinned at 0 and the other rows are free.

Missing values

Dummies are built from the full column before rows with missing values are dropped, and a missing value in the factor drops the row once:

dat_na <- dat
dat_na$group[c(3, 40)] <- NA
fit_na <- suppressMessages(fit_sem(paste0(base, "ab := a * b"), dat_na))
c(rows_used = fit_na@n_obs, rows_dropped = fit_na@n_dropped)
   rows_used rows_dropped
         398            2

A level that occurs only in dropped rows gives a dummy with no variation, and the fit stops with a message that names the dummy.

Fixed covariates, tests and refits

fixed_x = "group" fixes every dummy at its sample moments, and a dummy name fixes one. mbco_sem() refits through a stored factor map, so the data it needs is already in the fit:

mbco_sem(fit, paths = c("a", "b"))

    Minimum-of-two likelihood-ratio tests (MBCO) for an indirect effect

data:  a * b = 0
MBCO = 28.121, df = 1, p-value = 1.14e-07

Products and the four-way decomposition

group:mediator1 expands to one product per dummy, each a product term under the rules in the native model page. The fit warns that the global test is not valid with a product, so the chunk silences it and asks for the sandwich:

prod <- suppressWarnings(fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + group
  outcome_int ~ b * mediator1 + treatment + group + group:mediator1
", dat, se_type = "sandwich"))
tidy(prod)[grepl(":", tidy(prod)$term, fixed = TRUE) & tidy(prod)$op == "~", c("term", "estimate")]
# A tibble: 2 × 2
  term                             estimate
  <chr>                               <dbl>
1 outcome_int~group_mid:mediator1    0.0219
2 outcome_int~group_high:mediator1   0.0139

A factor covariate in the mediator equation works with the four-way decomposition, entering the covariate means through its dummies:

fw <- suppressWarnings(fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ treatment + group
  outcome_int ~ treatment + mediator1 + treatment:mediator1 + covariate2
", dat, se_type = "sandwich"))
tidy(extract_mediation(fw, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
                       decomposition = "four_way"), type = "components")[, 1:3]
# A tibble: 4 × 3
  term    estimate std_error
  <chr>      <dbl>     <dbl>
1 cde       0.0423    0.119
2 int_ref   0.0540    0.0380
3 int_med   0.273     0.0749
4 pie       0.392     0.0837

Limits

  • A categorical outcome, mediator or treatment is not supported in the native engine: only a covariate on a regression’s right side is expanded. The supported routes today:
    • A two-level treatment or mediator: recode it as a 0/1 numeric column.
    • A treatment with more than two levels: compare two levels at a time. Keep the rows of those two levels and code the pair 0/1; each comparison is one ordinary fit. There is no single set of effects for all levels yet.
    • A binary or count outcome or mediator: use fit_mediation(engine = "glm") with a binomial or poisson family. Ordinal variables are not supported by any medfit engine.
    These are on the roadmap as separate items, not scheduled.
  • A label, fixed value, start or bound on the factor stops (b*group); put it on one dummy. A constraint names the label, never the factor or a bare dummy.
  • Ordered factors, a one-level factor, a level that makes an invalid name, and a product of two categorical columns each stop with a message that says why. The full list of messages is in the Troubleshooting guide and in ?"medfit-syntax".
  • A refit from raw data (a nonparametric bootstrap that calls fit_sem() on each resample) rebuilds the factor each time, so a level missing from a character column’s resample changes the reference level.
